kind: T3 response to T7's regression-identifiability audit (acceptance + one additional cut)

acceptance.verdict: ACCEPTED in full. My cycle-12/13 wording is downgraded as T7 recommends: (a) 'COMPUTE TERM RESOLVED' -> compute 24.1 ms is the BEST-SUPPORTED WORKING VALUE (non-overlapping anchor-reproduction bands 12.52-12.87 vs 13.54-13.95 tok/s over the miss interval + the 410-bin identity), NOT statistically certified — the regression intercept alone cannot separate 18.1/24.1 (both fixed terms inside the 95% interval 22.84-55.65); (b) 'every constant measured or measured-confirmed' -> withdrawn; the evidence hierarchy is now stated per-constant below; (c) the fitted slope is a DESCRIPTIVE physical-MB association, not a directly measured logical-miss cost.
acceptance.unchanged: the regression remains a real measured association (17 points, R2 0.66); the microbench (A/B/install/sync), the source read, and the anchor reproduction stand as separate evidence lines.

additional_cut_slope_value.question: does the observed slope VALUE discriminate pure byte-service from per-miss (io+install) cost?
additional_cut_slope_value.pure_byte_service_at_measured_drive_rate: 0.179-0.263 ms/MB (1/5.59 to 1/3.82 GB/s, microbench bulk96 to k=1 step rate)
additional_cut_slope_value.reading: the observed slope sits ABOVE every pure-rate value and within 3% of the serial io+install prediction; but it is within 1 SE of the slowest measured rate (0.263), so this cut SUPPORTS a per-miss overhead beyond bytes without proving it. Marginal, honest.
additional_cut_slope_value.attribution_caveat: converting the slope to a per-EXPERT cost (0.797 ms) assumes physical~logical bytes; mincore bounds that error at <=3.2% IF the snapshot represents decode-time cache state — that premise is exactly T6's active stock-vs-flow audit; flagged as the dependency.

logical misses in [50.8, 53.5]/tok (mincore-bounded, pending T6 stock-vs-flow)
